tierMapping.vocabularyMismatchFound: GateFrontAccessTier (public-free|public-paid|platform-internal|tenant-private, gate-front-context.ts) is a CALL-CLASSIFICATION axis designed for the gate-front trust boundary (is this call anonymous/free, paid, an internal platform job, or a tenant-private integrated-product call) -- it is NOT the P-119 subscription ladder (Solo/Solo-annual/Studio/Studio-annual/Team/Team-annual/Property-Unlock). The dispatch's phrase 'which of the four existing access-tier values denotes Studio-or-better' assumes a closer mapping than the code actually has. Both real callers today (PE BFF and smartsite-mcp) already resolve the P-119 ladder LOCALLY (requireStudioSession; canRunStudioReport+hasPropertyUnlock) before ever building the outbound header, and both currently collapse every entitled outcome onto the single value 'public-paid' -- there is no live example of 'platform-internal' or 'tenant-private' being sent to this route today.
tierMapping.p119Source: 08_tiered_access_model.md (portfolio tier doc) + OPS-16_texas_market_plan_of_record.md row P-119 (operator's verbatim package table, 2026-09-05): Feasibility Studies appear on the Studio, Studio-annual, Team, Team-annual and Property-Unlock rows; Solo and Solo-annual do NOT include Feasibility Studies (only Property X-ray and Flood & Drainage). This is the authoritative ladder; P-119 is out of scope to re-litigate per the dispatch.

proposedAllowlist.rationale: Fail-closed default (refuse unless a recognized non-free value is present) collapses to a one-value blocklist given only four possible values, framed as an allowlist for correctness under future additions. public-paid is the value both current entitled callers actually send. platform-internal (an internal Hauska job/pipeline) and tenant-private (a paying SmartCity-OS-class tenant) are included on the reasoning that neither is the free/anonymous surface, but NEITHER IS EXERCISED BY ANY LIVE CALLER TODAY -- flagged as OPEN QUESTION Q2 below rather than decided unilaterally, since it is a judgment call this lane should not make silently on a security-relevant row.

tierMapping.signedContextPrecedence: Per the dispatch instruction 'the header is not trusted on its own where a signed context exists': when c.get('gateContextVerified') is present (HMAC-verified successfully via verifyGateContext, regardless of the transport-level gateContextMode being 'log' vs 'enforce' -- those two are orthogonal, gateContextMode only controls whether the OUTER request is rejected for a missing/invalid signature, not whether a valid payload's tier is honored downstream), the composer uses gateContextVerified.payload.tier instead of gateFront.accessTier. CONFIRMED BY GREP: no caller in either of this lane's two repos (legacy-design-tools, hauska-engine) currently mints x-hauska-gate-context/x-hauska-gate-signature -- this branch is real, tested, and forward-compatible, but INERT in production today. Stating this precisely so the close does not overclaim a live control.

sectionLevel.shape: absent(kind, reason, consequence) using the SAME FeasibilityFactState<ParcelOwnershipFacts> discriminated union every other absence in this file already uses -- never a null, never a second ad hoc shape.
sectionLevel.openDesignQuestion_Q1: feasibility-model.ts's AbsenceKind is a CLOSED, deliberately curated 5-value enum (clear|not-applicable|out-of-scope|blocked-at-source|failed-this-run) whose own docstring states 'a new producer cannot skip the question' of which kind of nothing was found -- none of the five mean 'the data exists and is known, but the caller is not entitled to see it' (an access-control fact, not a data-coverage fact). Recommendation: add a 6th kind, e.g. 'entitlement-required', rather than overload 'out-of-scope' (whose documented meaning is 'a scope decision... a sales conversation, not a defect' -- close, but conflates 'we chose not to build this' with 'you have not paid for this'). DEV_PROCESS 'an instrument's exclusion set is part of its contract' is exactly on point for this decision -- asking rather than deciding unilaterally.

topLevelMarker.purpose: So a caller does not have to diff which section changed to detect the refusal, add a same-response typed marker to the feasibility-export GET status/atom response (never changing the 200/201/202 status codes P-155's async job contract already commits to).
topLevelMarker.proposedShape: { ...existingResponse, entitlement: { tier: GateFrontAccessTier, granted: boolean, requiredTier: "studio-or-property-unlock", gatedSections: ["parcelOwnership"] } }
topLevelMarker.openDesignQuestion_Q4: Keep 200/201/202 + typed marker (my recommendation -- preserves 'every outcome carries the same declared envelope' from P-155), or introduce a distinct status/shape for the refused case? A 403 would break feasibility-export.ts's readStatus() which currently treats any non-res.ok as a generic upstream_error, losing the typed distinction MCP needs to re-wrap correctly.

mcpSideChanges_step3Preview.buildEngineGateHeaders: Currently hardcodes 'x-hauska-access-tier':'public-paid' in engine-client.ts for every feasibility call. Proposed: accept the caller's SmartsiteEntitlementSnapshot and derive the header value -- 'public-paid' when canRunStudioReport(entitlement) is true OR a live property-unlock was found for this parcel (both cases already gate entry to this call site today, so this is a consistency fix, not a new decision); the header should never be reached at all for a refused caller, since tools.ts's local gate already returns upgrade_required before feasibility-export.ts is invoked -- so in practice the header value does not change for the ONE path that calls it today. contradicted: 'smartsite-mcp has NO entitlement check before calling the engine' (P-152 lane 3 leave_behind, repeated verbatim in this dispatch's 'What is true today'): FALSE as stated for the ONLY code path that actually reaches the engine. tools.ts's export_instrument handler (kind=feasibility/siteplan/terrain/dossier, lines 1044-1088) already runs canRunStudioReport/canRunDeepReport + hasPropertyUnlock BEFORE calling out. What is actually missing, precisely: the ENGINE has no server-side enforcement of its own (confirmed live -- see the GET probe below), so the MCP's local check is necessary but not sufficient; a caller that reaches hauska-engine-api directly (bypassing MCP) is not gated by anything today.

The dispatch's step-4 live-violation instrument ('call run_report and get_smart_site for 48021:34049... paste the refusals... with the operator's Studio key, paste the values') targets the wrong tools for this lane's change. Both run_report and get_smart_site call cortex-api's POST /api/property-explorer/v1/research/brief (legacy-design-tools), which reads LDT's own Postgres fact atoms directly and is gated by its OWN pre-existing, independent mechanism (requirePePaidOrPropertyUnlocked + grantsCadRollValuationFor/studioGatedOwnerFactRefusal) -- NEITHER TOOL EVER CALLS hauska-engine-api. Building or testing the engine gate will produce zero observable change on either tool. The correct live-violation target for this lane is export_instrument with kind:'feasibility' (the sole MCP->engine-api direct call path); dossier/siteplan/terrain proxy through hauska-mcp-server, a third repo (SUBSTRATE seat) outside this lane's two registered repos. Recommend the planner correct the mission's step 4 before CP2, or explicitly accept that run_report/get_smart_site cannot demonstrate this lane's work.

outOfScopeFindingsForPlanner.relationToThisLane: The composer-level tier gate this lane builds meaningfully closes the gap for the two known legitimate callers (whose local checks were already correct) but does NOT stop a caller who hand-sets x-hauska-access-tier:public-paid directly against the public URL -- that requires mounting ENGINE_API_GATE_TOKEN (already coded, just unconfigured) and/or removing allUsers from the Cloud Run IAM policy, both of which are credential/infra changes of the kind the operational addendum reserves for planner/operator sign-off, not a lane's own judgment call.
outOfScopeFindingsForPlanner.recommendation: Flag as a follow-on row; do not fold into this lane without explicit planner instruction, since it changes blast radius (a live secret mount + an IAM policy change on a production service touched by two sibling lanes this wave) beyond 'gate two composers'.

openQuestionsForPlanner.Q1_absenceKind: Add a 6th AbsenceKind ('entitlement-required' or similar) to feasibility-model.ts's closed enum, or reuse 'out-of-scope'? Recommend adding a new kind; asking because DEV_PROCESS treats an instrument's exclusion set as part of its contract.
openQuestionsForPlanner.Q2_tierAllowlist: Grant on {public-paid, platform-internal, tenant-private}, refuse only on {public-free}? Neither platform-internal nor tenant-private is exercised by any live caller today. Confirm this is the intended posture, or specify a narrower allowlist (e.g. public-paid only, requiring platform-internal/tenant-private callers to separately prove entitlement some other way).
openQuestionsForPlanner.Q3_propertyUnlockGranularity: The engine's tier-only gate cannot distinguish 'Studio subscription' from 'one-off property-unlock for THIS parcel' the way MCP's own hasPropertyUnlock check can -- both currently arrive at the engine as the same 'public-paid' value. This is inherent to a header-only design and matches the already-accepted PE BFF pattern; flagging so it is a known, accepted limitation rather than a silent gap.
openQuestionsForPlanner.Q4_refusalTransport: Keep 200/201/202 + a typed in-body entitlement marker (recommended), or introduce a distinct status/shape for the engine's own refusal?
openQuestionsForPlanner.Q5_unauthenticatedEngine: See outOfScopeFindingsForPlanner above -- separate row, or extend this lane?
